title: The Farmer Who Kept Falling — Giddiness, Numb Feet, and Sugars That Wouldn't Behave

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 55 years old, a farmer, and he came in with four days of giddiness and generalized weakness, alongside vomiting that had actually started a day earlier. He'd been fine five days before, then began vomiting four to five times — food contents, non-bilious, non-projectile, each episode preceded by nausea. Four days ago he had an episode of giddiness with a fall, though he never lost consciousness and recovered on his own. He also describes a week of low-grade, intermittent fever with chills that responded to medication.

Alongside all this, he mentions his urination had increased but has now settled down, and he's been drinking a lot — about three jugs a day — and eating more than usual. A burning sensation in his feet, which he'd had before, has now subsided, but a tingling in both feet has been present for three years and became bad enough that he couldn't walk for the past week. He also gets giddy specifically after standing up. His vision has been blurry for three years — he has cataracts in both eyes — and he describes a strange "cotton wool" sensation under his feet when walking, also for three years. He denies any burning with urination.

He has also had breathlessness for four years, slowly worsening from mild exertion to more significant activity, though without needing to sit up at night or waking up breathless. No chest pain, palpitations, leg swelling, facial puffiness, cough, or loose stools.

His medical history is significant: he has had diabetes for 8 years, though no hypertension, coronary disease, or epilepsy. He's had two diabetic foot ulcers requiring surgery — right foot in 2013, left foot in 2017. Just a month before this admission, he was hospitalized for deviation of his mouth to the right side, slurred speech, and poorly controlled sugars, and was sent home on NPH and Actrapid insulin. But he stopped the insulin himself two days before this admission and switched to oral medications on his own.

He has been drinking about 90 mL of alcohol daily for 30 years, though he stopped a month ago. He does not smoke and has no known allergies.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General appearance:** conscious, coherent, cooperative, moderately built and nourished; no pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, or lymphadenopathy
- **Vitals:** BP 120/80 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, RR 16/min, temp 97.8°F, random blood glucose 216 mg/dL
- **Respiratory and abdominal exam:** unremarkable — trachea central, vesicular breath sounds, soft non-tender abdomen
- **Cardiovascular exam:** normal heart sounds, no murmurs
- **Neurological exam:**
  - Higher mental functions, orientation, speech, memory, and cranial nerves all intact
  - Motor system: normal bulk and tone in upper limbs; increased tone (hypertonia) in both lower limbs, thought to be voluntary; power reduced to 4/5 in all four limbs
  - All deep tendon reflexes and the abdominal reflex were absent
  - Sensory system: fine touch absent in both hands up to the wrists and both feet up to the ankles; vibration sense absent in both arms up to the elbows and both legs up to the knees
  - No cerebellar signs — finger-nose, heel-knee, and rapid alternating movements were all normal
